nodes.name: FeOOH-MOF/NF solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.375 mmol of FeCl2·4H2O and 0.2 mmol of BDC were dissolved in a mixture composed of 10.0 mL HCON(CH3)2, 1.0 mL CH3CH2OH, and 1.0 mL DI water, and then transferred to a 20 mL polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reactor. Subsequently, the washed NF strip was placed in the reactor, which was sealed and maintained at 120°C for 3 h. Finally, the resulting sample was washed with DI water and CH3CH2OH, dried and named FeOOH-MOF/NF.

nodes.name: (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF corrosion treatment
nodes.procedure: The FeOOH-MOF/NF was immersed in 10.0 mL of 0.1 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O solution and allowed to undergo spontaneous reaction (i.e., corrosion) at RT for 12 h, after which the samples were thoroughly washed with DI water, dried overnight in an oven at 60°C and subsequently designated as the (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF.

nodes.description: OER stability at 710 mA/cm² in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF only requires an overpotential of 314 mV to achieve a high current density of 710 mA cm⁻², and no significant degradation is observed after 120 h of operation.
the Faraday efficiency (FE) tests show that the actual O₂ volumes collected at 100 mA cm⁻² are close to the theoretical values (Fig. 5d)

a two-electrode cell was constructed using (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF and Pt sheet as the anode and cathode... only requires a 1.86 V (without iR-compensation) voltage to reach 500 mA cm⁻². Furthermore, the chronopotentiometric test shows that the cell requires only 1.95 V to maintain a current density of 500 mA cm⁻², and no significant degradation was observed over 120 h
multiple current step tests indicate that the stability of (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF is hardly affected by current fluctuations (Fig. 5c)

nodes.characterization_summary: FeOOH-MOF shows FeOOH phase (PDF#18-0639) peaks and MOF-74 peaks. (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF shows additional NiOOH phase (PDF#27-0956) peaks with lower crystallinity due to defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks positioned at 18.0°, 33.2°, 35.6°, 40.9°, 49.7°, 62.5° and 63.8° are attributed to the FeOOH phase (PDF #18-0639) (marked by yellow squares) ... the NiOOH phase was formed, with characteristic diffraction peaks located at 28.9°, 35.7°, 54.3°, 62.6°, and 64.3° (PDF#27–0956) (marked with green pentagons). Notably, the (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF has lower crystallinity compared to FeOOH-MOF

nodes.characterization_summary: FeOOH-MOF/NF shows rough surface with regular parallelogram lamellae. (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF shows uniform nanosheet arrays coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 2a-b, the FeOOH-MOF/NF surface has a rough texture with regular parallelogram lamellae. However, after the corrosion treatment, the surface of the obtained (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF was uniformly coated with nanosheet arrays (Fig. 2c-d)

nodes.characterization_summary: (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF confirms nanosheet structure with HRTEM showing (031) FeOOH plane at 0.218 nm and (211) NiOOH plane at 0.167 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM results further confirm the nanosheet structure of the (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF obtained (Fig. 2f-g). Notably, the two crystal planes, i.e., (031) and (211), are clearly visible in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image ... with lattice spacings of 0.218 nm and 0.167 nm, respectively.

N₂ adsorption-desorption isothermal tests show that the specific surface area and pore volume of the FeOOH-MOF/NF are 317.9 m² g⁻¹ and 0.1 cm³ g⁻¹, respectively, while those of the (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF are greatly decreased to 3.0 m² g⁻¹ and 0.05 cm³ g⁻¹, respectively (Figure S2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeOOH-MOF/NF: Ni 2p (Ni²⁺ 856.0/873.4 eV, Ni³⁺ 874.9/857.6 eV, 5.04% Ni³⁺), Fe 2p (Fe²⁺ 711.7/722.8 eV, Fe³⁺ 715.3/724.6 eV), O 1s (Ov 530.9 eV). (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF: Ni³⁺ peak shifts +0.5 eV, Fe³⁺ shifts -0.7 eV, Ni³⁺ 9.75%, O 1s shifts -1.0 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface chemistry of the FeOOH-MOF/NF and (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF was analyzed using XPS technique. Fig. 3a shows the highresolution spectra of the Ni 2p for FeOOH-MOF/NF, where two peaks located at 856.0 eV and 873.4 eV are attributed to the Ni²⁺ ... Compared to FeOOH-MOF/NF, the binding energy peak of Ni³⁺ in (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF is positively shifted by 0.5 eV, whereas the binding energy peak of Fe³⁺ is negatively shifted by 0.7 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeOOH-MOF/NF: Ov as lattice electron trapping sites (g=2.081). (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF: Ov as surface electron trapping sites (g=2.005).
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further confirm the presence of Ov in FeOOH-MOF/NF and (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF, EPR tests were performed. As shown in Fig. 3e, Ov exists as a lattice electron trapping sites (g = 2.081) in FeOOH-MOF/NF, whereas it exists as a surface electron trapping sites (g = 2.005) in (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF (Fig. 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: (Fe,Ni)OOH-MOF/NF shows uniform distribution of C, O, Ni, and Fe elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) results show a uniform distribution of C, O, Ni, and Fe (Fig. 2e).
